title: A Novel Approach for Identical Location Transmission Electron Microscopy Characterization in Harsh Electrochemical Environments
content: In situ electrochemical liquid cell transmission electron microscopy (EC-TEM) enables real-time observation of the structural, morphological, and compositional evolution of catalysts in working environment during electrochemical reactions [1]. It is a powerful tool for studying electrocatalysis. However, its application is constrained by the limited stability of the liquid cell over prolonged reaction time in hash conditions. To overcome this limitation, identical location TEM (IL-TEM) serves as a valuable complementary technique for studying the evolution of electrocatalysts under long-term operating conditions, allowing nanoscale observation of catalysts at the same location over extended periods [2]. In this approach, catalysts are typically deposited onto a carbon film supported-Au grid, which serves as the working electrode in oxygen evolution reaction (OER) studies. By imaging the same sample area before and after reactions, IL-TEM enables precise tracking of structural and compositional changes while minimizing the continuous electron beam interactions with the catalyst and the liquid electrolyte to avoid sample degradation and potential beam induced artifacts. However, during the OER reactions the gas evolution and the high anodic potential can lead to the degradation of commonly used carbon-coated grids, while the continuous dissolution of Au above 1.5 V verses the Reversible Hydrogen Electrode (VRHE) and its subsequent precipitation on the catalyst may compromise the reliability of catalyst evaluation [3]. It is essential to address these challenges for the robustness of IL-TEM methods in these important applications.
